surface: SUNNYVAiLE NewsStand / The Daily / Career / Work-Life

readerContract.humanQuestion: How can I prepare for a difficult work conversation when I do not feel confident yet?
readerContract.promisedPayoff: Choose one bounded conversation, prepare a truthful first line and rehearse one realistic objection without mistaking practice for prediction.
readerContract.priorKnowledge: The reader knows what an AI chat tool is but may not have used a spoken conversation mode.
readerContract.centralMentalModel: Career preparation can begin before confidence arrives; an AI can supply practice turns but cannot understand the real person or situation.
readerContract.dailyLifeConnection: A necessary deadline or expectations conversation that has stayed on the calendar because its opening feels uncomfortable.
readerContract.surfaceJob: One compact Career / Work-Life item whose non-AI advice stands alone before an earned AI connection.
readerContract.desiredFeeling: I know the first small move and where the tool stops being useful.

canonicalTruth.freshnessTrigger: Clark changes the post, OpenAI changes Voice or its data controls, a different provider is named, or the use expands beyond low-stakes rehearsal.

strengthsToUse: answer the actual reader problem quickly
separate the supported method from its limits
give one specific action without overclaiming

draftArchitecture.plainAnswer: Do not wait for confidence: choose one bounded conversation, write its purpose and first honest sentence, then rehearse one likely objection.
causalSequence: Waiting for confidence postpones the necessary conversation.
A clear purpose and first sentence lower the preparation burden.
One rehearsal makes the first exchange concrete and exposes wording to improve.
The real conversation still requires human judgment about the person, power and consequences.
draftArchitecture.workedCase: A deadline conversation begins: I want to understand why the deadline moved and agree on what we can still deliver. Could we walk through what changed?
draftArchitecture.transferCase: A promotion-scope conversation begins with the result sought, one factual opening and one likely objection, without asking the tool to predict the manager.
draftArchitecture.usefulAction: Choose one bounded conversation, write the first line and rehearse one round.

analogyPlan.analogy: A rehearsal partner, not an office oracle
analogyPlan.mapping: The AI supplies one practice objection and waits for the users response.
analogyPlan.limit: The practice turn does not model the actual persons motives, power or likely response.
analogyPlan.whyItHelps: It makes the tools small job visible while preventing the reader from treating generated dialogue as a forecast.

humourPlan.lessonJob: The office-oracle line makes the prediction boundary memorable without turning the advice into a joke.

draftArchitecture.formatSpecificStructure: Recognizable delayed conversation; useful non-AI advice and wording; explicit AI rehearsal method; privacy and judgment boundary; one try-today move.
draftArchitecture.antiTemplateDecision: No generic confidence slogan, management maxim, AI-first headline, magic prompt, check-the-receipts repetition or Promptoscope frame.

communicationDesign.surfaceAdaptation: Start with the delayed human conversation, make one preparation move concrete, introduce AI only as a bounded rehearsal partner, then land on the human decision boundary.

humanQuestion.reason: The reader recognizes a necessary conversation delayed while she waits to feel confident.
humanQuestion.plannedEvidence: The opening names the conversation still sitting on the calendar.

usefulCuriosity.reason: The useful shift is from waiting for a feeling to preparing the first exchange.
usefulCuriosity.plannedEvidence: The prose separates confidence from a purpose and truthful first sentence.

invisibleProcessConcrete.reason: Rehearsal can otherwise sound like vague role-play.
invisibleProcessConcrete.plannedEvidence: The AI raises one likely objection at a time and pauses while the reader answers.

familiarTechnicalMovement.reason: A moved-deadline conversation gives the method an ordinary professional setting.
familiarTechnicalMovement.plannedEvidence: The worked wording names the outcome and asks what changed.

limitationsConsequences.reason: The generated response cannot represent the real person or make a high-stakes situation safe.
limitationsConsequences.plannedEvidence: The boundary names power, fairness, safety, law and confidentiality.

humourSurprise.reason: One compact line can preserve the prediction boundary.
humourSurprise.plannedEvidence: The AI is a rehearsal partner, not the office oracle.

betterNextQuestion.reason: The reader needs a small preparation question rather than a promise of confidence.
betterNextQuestion.plannedEvidence: The closing asks which sentence she wants ready when the real conversation begins.

explanationArc.adaptation: The compact service item gives useful career guidance first, uses only enough mechanism to explain the rehearsal and ends with one action.

representativeProofPlan.highestRisk: Repeating generic management advice or introducing AI before the Career / Work-Life guidance can stand alone.
representativeProofPlan.plannedProof: The exact headline and complete prefix before the explicit AI connection must remain useful non-AI career guidance, followed by one followable rehearsal and an honest limit.
representativeProofPlan.acceptanceOutcome: A non-technical reader can state the first preparation step, use the tool for one practice turn and explain why it cannot predict or judge the real conversation.
